RATIONALE:
Q1: Option A won't reliably work. A public report from an Ubuntu 26.04 runner (safeinsights/canopycms#1106) shows uutils `cat` returning 0 after its reader had gone, even with an input twice `fs.pipe-max-size`, so a bigger payload in `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py:228-243` would probably still fail. Option C would drop the documented `gh_retry` contract in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1196-1198` ("the copy's non-zero status is returned and the command is not re-run"), and D would fail again on re-run. So change the replay at `scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1229` so it no longer relies on coreutils `cat` to report a closed reader. Keep these properties: output stays byte-exact (NUL bytes and a missing trailing newline included, see `test_first_try_success_passes_stdout_through_unchanged`); the caller's own shell is not killed (write from a subshell); the status is non-zero whenever not every byte is delivered, whether SIGPIPE is default or ignored; and the successful command is never re-run. Leave the existing test unchanged. Add deterministic tests that don't depend on the runner's coreutils: one defines a shell function `cat` that reads all input and returns 0, the way uutils `cat` behaves, and checks that the closed-reader case still gives `_calls == 1` and a non-zero rc; another runs the same case under `trap '' PIPE`.
Q2: GITHUB FACTS show PR #9218 is open and changes only the collector, its test, the docs and a changelog fragment. The failing test `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py` runs in the "Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests" step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:882`) and covers `scripts/gh_helpers.sh`, which #9218 doesn't touch, so the failure comes from main, not from #9218. The fix goes in its own PR against the default branch, as the pipeline normally does. That PR must not re-run, comment on or change PR #9218.
